correctness.rationale: For each n with at least n support points, pairwise disjoint Urysohn bumps span an isometric copy of ell-infinity^n on which J_mu is isometric. Every rank-<n operator has a nonzero kernel vector on this subspace, giving the lower bound 1; the zero approximant gives the upper bound. If the support has m<n points, L-infinity(mu) has dimension m and J_mu has rank below n. The zero-measure case is immediate.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete exact approximation-number classification for a natural canonical operator. It isolates a genuine L-infinity endpoint effect: any infinite support, including a purely atomic one, forces every finite-index approximation number to equal the operator norm. This sharply differs from finite-exponent compactness criteria that depend on diffuse mass and is useful for deciding exactly when finite-rank approximation can improve the norm.
